The question

Who toured, and then heard nothing useful from us

You asked for every family that toured in the last 45 days with no completed follow-up, no date-specific next step and no other decision-maker engaged. Then, which of them had several conversations with us before they went quiet, what they have in common, and where this happens most.

The short answer. 102 families toured in the last 45 days and 87 are still open. 34 of those 87 meet all three conditions. 24 of the 34 had 3 or more two-way conversations with us, the tour included, and then went quiet. In 23 of those 24, the family named another person who will help decide, and nobody contacted that person. The breakdown is most common at Pine Harbor (11 of 21 open families) and in agency referrals (15 of 27), and it happens right after the first tour.

"Completed follow-up" means a two-way conversation after the tour: a call that reached the family, a reply to an email or text, or a home visit. A voicemail or an unanswered text is an attempt, not a completed follow-up.

Question 3

What the 24 quiet families have in common

Each pattern compares the 24 families that went quiet with the 53 open toured families that are still moving (a completed follow-up, a dated next step or a second decision-maker engaged).

Another decision-maker was named, and nobody called them.

Named another decision-maker during the tour
Went quiet
24 families
23 (96%)
Still moving
53 families
21 (40%)
Families   Named another decision-maker

23 of the 24 quiet families told us during the tour about a son, a sister or a spouse who will help decide, often one who lives in another city or holds power of attorney. The CRM has no contact with any of them. Among families still moving, 40% named another decision-maker, and in those families someone usually reached that person or booked a dated next step.

Possible explanation, not established: the primary contact may be waiting for that person before replying. What the data cannot show: conversations that happened and were not logged.

After the tour, we left messages but did not talk.

For all 24 quiet families, every contact after the tour was a voicemail, a text or an email with no reply. 20 of the 24 (83%) got their first post-tour attempt three or more days after the tour, against 21% of families still moving. Before the tour, the same families answered calls and replied to emails; 17 of them had four or more conversations with us.

Possible explanation, not established: the window after the tour is when families compare options, and a later first attempt reaches them after that. Small counts: treat this as a pattern to check, not a rate to plan on.

Price came up on most tours, and no pricing was sent.

Pricing was discussed on the tour for 20 of the 24 quiet families. None of them has a pricing document or a pricing review logged after the tour. Among families still moving, 74% discussed price, so price alone does not separate the groups. What separates them is what happened next.

What looks healthy.

25 of the 53 families still moving (47%) have already reached a second visit or an assessment. Families with a dated next step are in every community and with every salesperson, so the practice exists across the team.

Method

How to read this report

Toured means a completed tour between September 14, 2026 and October 29, 2026. Open means not moved in and not closed. Completed follow-up is a two-way contact after the tour. Date-specific next step is a next step in the CRM with a date on or after today. Another decision-maker engaged means a logged contact with someone other than the main contact. Went quiet means 3 or more two-way conversations, the tour included, and none since the tour.

The findings describe patterns in CRM records. They do not establish cause, and they do not score families. Activity that was never logged looks the same as activity that never happened.
